Ligand 1 is the bromine molecule, Phi 2.3799, with atom 1 the carbonyl, atom 17 the cyclopropane CH, and the bromine at atom 12 on azine carbon 11. I am building the methylpyrazole-at-C4 design on an oxetane cap rather than a cyclopropyl, to hedge the cap choice while the aryl results are still unscored. Order matters here: I swap the cap first, because going from a three- to a four-membered ring inserts one atom after position 16 and leaves the azine numbering untouched, so the second cut's indices stay valid. Doing it the other way round would shift everything by five.

Now the azine. Atom 11 still carries the bromine at atom 12, and I replace it with the 1-methylpyrazol-4-yl. A benzene there was worth 0.70 against bromine's 0.60, and the pyrazole keeps the flat aromatic while being far more polar. Combined with the oxetane this is the least lipophilic way I can present that ring: about 349 Da at LogP near 2.6, where the phenyl original sat above 5. If the aryl effect survives this much nitrogen, QED should land in the mid 0.8s and the molecule clears 2.42.
